title: Mcp Apps
motto: Text-only tool output caps what agents can show. MCP Apps (SEP-1724, official January 26, 2026) let a tool return sandboxed interactive HTML rendered inline in Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Goose, and VS Code. Dashboards, forms, maps, 3D scenes, all through one extension. This lesson walks the `ui://` resource scheme, the `text/html;profile=mcp-app` MIME, the iframe-sandbox postMessage protocol, and the security surface that comes with letting a server render HTML.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Text-only tool output caps what agents can show. MCP Apps (SEP-1724, official January 26, 2026) let a tool return sandboxed interactive HTML rendered inline in Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Goose, and VS Code. Dashboards, forms, maps, 3D scenes, all through one extension. This lesson walks the `ui://` resource scheme, the `text/html;profile=mcp-app` MIME, the iframe-sandbox postMessage protocol, and the security surface that comes with letting a server render HTML.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: A 2025-era `visualize_timeline` tool can return "Here are 14 notes organized chronologically: ...". That is a paragraph. Users actually want the interactive timeline. Before MCP Apps, the options were: client-specific widget APIs (Claude artifacts, OpenAI Custom GPT HTML), or no UI at all.

MCP Apps (SEP-1724, shipped January 26, 2026) standardize the contract. A tool result contains a `resource` whose URI is `ui://...` and whose MIME is `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. The host renders it in a sandboxed iframe with a limited CSP and no network access unless explicitly granted. The UI inside the iframe posts messages to the host via a tiny postMessage JSON-RPC dialect.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: MCP Apps embed interactive UIs in tool responses.
